/LILIAN

HAPPY MID- AUTUMN FESTIVAL!

Baltic Exchange Market Report 24 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3473 (43)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5939 (78)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2382 (49)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1782 (4)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1003 (1)
CAPESIZE
The Capesize market continued its ascent towards the highs seen earlier this month, with the BCI 182 5TC rising a further $709 to close at $53,864. In contrast to yesterday, strength in the Atlantic basin more than compensated for losses in the Pacific. Anticipation had been building throughout the week in the Atlantic amid growing cargo volumes and increasing talk of tightening tonnage availability in the North Atlantic. As the weekend approached, both transatlantic and fronthaul routes finally surged. Backed by a series of strong overnight fixtures, the C8 route jumped $6,000 to $64,250, its highest level since early December last year. The C9 route moved in the same direction though to a lesser extent, gaining $2,222 to $91,639. The sharp rise in C8 continued to underpin C9, with the stronger earnings available on the transatlantic route helping to drive sentiment on the latter. The West Australia to Qingdao activity remained in the Pacific. The C5 index slipped below $16 after fixtures reportedly concluded in the high $15s by two miners.

Atlantic
An unnamed Newcastlemax from Oldendorff linked to 170,000/10 Seven Islands to Qingdao 19/26 October at $47.00. Cargill took the Genco Intrepid (180,007 2016) for 140,000/10 Seven Islands to Djen Djen 16/22 October at $27.25. Vale took the CS Wu Han (179,692 2021) for 170,000/10 Seven Islands to Praia Mole 8/12 October at $26.50.

Asia
There was rumour of Rio Tinto and FMG fixing at $15.95 for 170,000/10 from Dampier 12/14 October and $160,000/10 from Port Hedland 9/10 October to Qingdao. The Lady Deena (182,588 2020) was fixed for 170,000/10 West Australia to China 12/14 October at around $16.75.
PANAMAX
The market improved across both basins today, with the P5TC increasing by $438 to $21,434. In the Atlantic, brokers reported clear signs of strengthening sentiment as bids for trans-Atlantic rounds moved higher, while market sources noted a tightening tonnage list off both the North Continent and West Mediterranean. As a result, Owners with prompt tonnage are increasingly able to push their rate ideas higher as market fundamentals shift further in their favour. The US Gulf was also described as more active, with improving fronthaul bids adding further support to sentiment. In the Pacific, activity also increased with stronger demand from Indonesia and firmer rates being discussed. Improving Atlantic conditions are providing additional support for Far East owners, as the option of ballasting to secure EC South America employment has become increasingly attractive. Demand from Australia and the North Pacific is reported to remain consistently steady, offering further support to rates. This growing confidence among Owners is, however, contributing to a wider bid-offer spread, with some market participants noting that negotiations are becoming more difficult to conclude. The Cassiopeia Ocean (82,069 2018) open CJK 28 September was reported as fixed, although no other details surfaced. Meanwhile, the Tai Knighthood (84,434 2021) open Taichung 24 September was reported to have been placed on subjects.
SUPRAMAX
Another day of minimal movement on the Index and the 11TC average up another $54 to settle at $22,525. The Atlantic appeared to be mostly flat with limited trading evident, however talk of Ultra scrap rates from the Continent to the East Mediterranean approaching $40,000 was a notable highlight. The South Atlantic remained steady, although limited demand in the West Mediterranean may now encourage ballasters, and demand also seemed thin from the US Gulf. There was more activity in Asia with continued NoPac fixing and Indonesia to India-Bangladesh being the main drivers, which has helped maintain period interest with the Subra (64,061 2024) North Vietnam early October reported fixed for 5 to7 months at $24,500 to Oldendorff. The Vimc Sunrise (56,057 2006) open Singapore 30 September-1 October fixed a trip via Indonesia to Thailand with coal in the $19,000’s and Teambulk were linked with a 57,000-dwt open South China for a clinker cargo to Chittagong at $29,000. A small Supra was said to be on subjects for a round voyage from East coast India via Bahudopi at $18,000 and the BT Trevia (63,581 2016) prompt Bataan did a trip via Indonesia back to the Far East with coal in the mid $18,000’s.
HANDYSIZE
The Handysize market recorded another mixed session, with sentiment largely shaped by positional factors. The BHSI closed at 1,003, while the 7TC average increased by $30 to finish at $18,061. The South Atlantic and US Gulf remained relatively quiet, with steady demand supporting firm rates. The Norse Kyushu (42,565 2026) open on the EC Central America was reported fixed by Oldendorff for a transatlantic trip at $27,000, although further details were not disclosed. Across the basin, both the Continent and Mediterranean continued to gain momentum, with scrap business fixing at particularly strong levels. The Queen Island (37,802 2018) open Gdansk on 2–7 October was heard fixed for a grains trip to the Mediterranean, although further details were not disclosed. The Asian market also experienced another quiet session, with the tonnage list appearing relatively longer while enquiries continued to be discussed at healthy levels.

Market Fundamentals
CISA Daily Crude Steel Production

In the period 11-20 September, daily crude steel production at China Iron and Steel Association (CISA) member mills eased 0.1% from the preceding ten days to 1.9 Mt/day, industry association data show. Meanwhile, output stood 7.3% lower than the same period last year.
Sent from Front

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape was heavy through the session after an early push above 50k in October. Oct 26 opened around 50,000–50,250 before slipping steadily, trading through 49,500 and later down to 47,750–48,000, with a small late bounce toward 48,500. Nov 26 eased from around 47,250 to 45,700–45,900, while Dec 26 softened from the mid-44s to around 43,750. Q4 26 traded from 47,400/47,250 early down toward 45,500–46,000 later.
